Request self-registration

Source: R/registration.R
aa_register_user.Rd

Checks the login, password, email and the domain and rate limits from the settings, and stores a pending registration with the password hash. With registration_verify_email = TRUE a one-time confirmation link is sent with settings$send_reset(email, link, login); with FALSE the account is created immediately. Only the token hash is stored in the database.

Usage

aa_register_user(conn, login, password, email, settings = aa_settings())

Arguments

conn

Connection with the aa_init_db() schema.

login

Desired login.

password

Desired password (only the hash is stored).

email

Email address of the visitor.

settings

Settings, the result of aa_settings() with registration_enabled = TRUE.

Value

A list (invisibly): sent, reason and login. Reasons: created, sent, disabled, user_exists, email_exists, email_invalid, registration_domain, registration_throttled, send_failed or a login or password validation reason.

Details

The result is meant for the journal and for choosing a generic on-screen answer: the reason user_exists or email_exists must not be shown to a visitor, because that would reveal which accounts exist.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("RSQLite", quietly = TRUE)) {
  conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
  aa_init_db(conn)
  aa_create_first_admin(conn, "boss", "boss-password")

  settings <- aa_settings(
    registration_enabled = TRUE,
    registration_verify_email = FALSE,
    registration_role = "viewer"
  )
  aa_register_user(conn, "worker", "worker-password", "worker@example.com",
                   settings)$reason
  aa_list_users(conn)
  DBI::dbDisconnect(conn)
}
